hooks.reason: Container-side CSS; each container (toolbar, banner, tab list) owns a `::slotted([data-tct-edge-comp]:first-child)` rule. There is no shared helper to port.

differences.text: The five content props (`content`, `header`, `footer`, `start`, `end`) are slots; `children` and `content` are the default slot. The regions are `tct-layout-header`, `-footer`, `-panel` and `-content` elements placed in those slots.

The area (start or end) of a panel comes from the slot it sits in, answered by handlers on the slot wrappers through the context protocol, because one provider cannot answer differently per slot. A region that connected before the layout rendered asks again when the layout announces itself in `firstUpdated`.
`data-tct-edge-comp` replaces the upstream edge compensation attribute; ghost buttons and tabs should reflect it (shared-file request).

`content-width` resolves with `100cqi` alignment arithmetic on a size container that exists only when a region needs it (`data-width-mode` none, constrained or internal). A number in the property is px.

requests.reason: Ghost buttons and tabs should reflect the passive attribute `data-tct-edge-comp` (EDGE_COMP_ATTR in layout/layout.types.ts) so containers (toolbar, banner, tab list) can pull them to the edge with `::slotted([data-tct-edge-comp]:first-child)`; the toolbar already reads it.

differences.text: `landmark` replaces `role` (a host `role` attribute would shadow the element role) and `label` names the inner scroller, which carries the role and the tab stop.
`no-scroll` replaces `isScrollable` (the default is scrolling on, so the attribute states the exception).

The scroller is keyboard reachable exactly while it overflows and nothing tabbable is inside (the core scrollable-area controller, owner `implicit`), instead of always. `focus()` on the host focuses the inner scroller.

A boolean attribute plus the configuration attributes `default-size`, `min-size`, `max-size`, `collapsible`, `collapsed-size`, `snaps`, `auto-save-id`, `container`, `collapsed`. The `region` property takes an external ResizableProps (a ResizableController) instead.

api.reason: A-xstyle: style the host, `::part(base)` or the documented attributes and custom properties.

differences.text: The `resizable` object prop is the boolean attribute `resizable` plus configuration attributes; the state lives in a controller the panel owns, and `region` (property) accepts an external one. A `tct-resize-handle` next to the panel (or with `for=<panel id>`) operates it.

`tct-size-change` (non-cancelable notification, `size`, `reason`) and `tct-collapse-change` (cancelable intent, `collapsed`, `reason`) replace the resize callbacks. They fire for pointer, keyboard and request changes and never for a programmatic `resize()` or `collapsed` write.

A collapsed panel is `visibility: hidden` with a zero inline size, so its content leaves the tab order and the accessibility tree (`:state(collapsed)`); upstream keeps a collapsed-width strip with clipped content.
The persisted size uses the `tct-resizable:` local-storage prefix.

core.layout-panel.notes: Guides: [mwg:css-layout] inline-size on the inner box, logical edges; [mwg:size-aware-styling] container basis for percentage sizes.
